name: scatter_khasi
description: Khasi — the language of the Khasi people of the Meghalaya hills (also Assam, Bangladesh), written in Roman (Sohra/Standard orthography) and Bengali; orthodoxy-classified under the Khasic branch of the same 'Austro-Asiatic' family as Munda, but geographically and structurally distant — the Meghalaya highlands rather than the central forest belt. On the standardized 12-column place axis. The defining structural feature of Khasi is the voiceless-aspirated stop contrast (pʰ, tʰ, kʰ) — the Mon-Khmer signature — which the Munda branches do not carry natively. NO retroflex stops or retroflex flap. Voiced stops are limited (b, d, g). Four matched nasals (m, n, ɲ, ŋ). Sibilant /s/, glottal /h/, glottal stop /ʔ/, lateral /l/, trill /r/, glides /w, j/. The voiceless-aspirated row plus the absent retroflex column places Khasi visibly outside the Munda template even under the same orthodox family label. Conservative inventory drawn from Henderson and Nagaraja; 20 cells filled.
